topic: Preparation Before Speaking & Clarification Under Time Pressure
newExpressions: I prefer to prepare before I speak because planning helps me be clear.
bestSentence: Last week I asked the exact scope and it saved time.
correctedSentence: I understand we're in a rush, but two minutes to confirm the scope could save us from rework.
feedback: You practiced giving an opinion with one reason, supporting it with a concrete example, and responding constructively when a manager pushes for speed. Your message became much clearer when you used short structures. The recurring problem was restarting and rebuilding the sentence when you tried to explain a more complex idea. Keep the structure simple: opinion, reason, example; then acknowledge, propose, benefit under pressure.
nextChallenge: Give a 60-second opinion on an unfamiliar topic, support it with one example, and handle one skeptical interruption using acknowledge, propose, and benefit without restarting.
selfCorrection: Partial. Short target sentences were repeated successfully, but longer answers still included restarts and reformulation.
repetitionResult: Successful on the core opinion sentence and the short example after modeling.
transferResult: Partial. The learner understood the acknowledge-propose-benefit structure, but the final pressured response remained unfinished.

lessonNote.finalVersion: I prefer to prepare before I speak because planning helps me organize my ideas and make my point clearer. For example, last week I clarified the exact scope before starting a task, and it saved us time. I know there are situations when we're in a rush, but even then a short clarification can be useful. Two minutes to confirm the scope could prevent much more rework later. So my approach is to prepare enough to be clear without letting preparation slow down the work.
